overview: Oman is a country on the south-eastern corner of the Arabian Peninsula. Its capital and largest city is Muscat. Oman is a sultanate and was once a great sea power whose lands stretched as far as Zanzibar in East Africa. Oil and gas are important to its economy.

geography.text: Most of Oman is desert, including part of the Rub' al Khali, or Empty Quarter. The Hajar Mountains rise in the north, and a long coastline faces the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman. The Musandam Peninsula, cut off from the rest of the country by the United Arab Emirates, overlooks the Strait of Hormuz, and the south around Salalah turns green during the summer monsoon.

history.text: Oman was a seafaring nation that traded across the Indian Ocean for centuries. After driving out the Portuguese in 1650, its sultans built an empire that included Zanzibar and parts of the East African coast. Sultan Qaboos, who came to power in 1970, used the country's oil wealth to modernise it.

events.title: Portuguese expelled
events.text: Omani forces drive the Portuguese out.

events.title: Court moves to Zanzibar
events.text: Sultan Said moves his capital to Zanzibar.

events.title: Sultan Qaboos
events.text: Qaboos bin Said begins modernising the country.

government.text: Oman is an absolute monarchy. The Sultan is head of state and government and holds most power. Sultan Qaboos ruled from 1970 to 2020, followed by his cousin Haitham bin Tariq. An elected Consultative Assembly advises the government.

economy.text: Oil and gas are Oman's main exports, but its reserves are smaller than its neighbours'. It is investing in tourism, logistics, fishing and green hydrogen.

culture.text: Oman has a long seafaring history, and traditional wooden boats called dhows are still built there. Frankincense trees grow in the south, and the incense trade made the region rich in ancient times. Forts and castles dot the country.

items.title: Frankincense
items.text: Aromatic resin traded for thousands of years.

items.title: Bahla Fort
items.text: A huge mud-brick fort listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Dhows
items.text: Wooden sailing ships used for trade across the Indian Ocean.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Oman has won the Arabian Gulf Cup twice. Sailing is also strong, and camel racing is a traditional pastime.

items.title: Camel racing
items.text: A traditional sport across the Gulf.
